answer: One defense is anchored commitments with delayed reveal. Each agent posts a hash of its identity key to a public atlas of registrations, then waits several epochs before the key is revealed and it can transact. Because entries sit visibly in the atlas during the delay, peers notice when a nebula of thousands of fresh commitments appears at once and discount that whole cohort. Speed buys the attacker nothing: every fake identity must age through the same waiting period, slow as water carving karst, with its bonded capital locked and slashable until the reveal clears.
